metadata.methods_description: EEG recordings were collected from 80 participants who completed an attitude assessment task followed by a visual judgment paradigm. Participants viewed protest photographs preceded by pie charts indicating varying levels of social support (low, medium, high) for sociopolitical issues, and subsequently rated their support for the protestors.

citation_details.title: Moral conviction and metacognitive ability shape multiple stages of information processing
citation_details.author: Keith J. Yoder, Jean Decety
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises human electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 80 participants engaged in a moral decision-making task. Participants evaluated their attitudes toward sociopolitical issues, then viewed protest photographs while receiving information about social support levels for each issue presented as pie charts (low, medium, high). The study investigates how moral conviction and metacognitive ability influence neural processing stages during social judgment and attitude formation.
